html:
SMTO-LLM-0074 — The model you picked isn't served at the address SMTO would use

GUID: 79c0ba55-cca9-5f88-8d04-82d3bb930f0f
Slug: local-ai-model-identity-mismatch
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • Before switching SMTO to this model, SMTO checked the model server from both the SMTO server and the Gateway. The model wasn't there, or the two checks saw different servers. Your current Main model hasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In a new message, ask SMTO to list the models served by your local AI profile, and copy the model's name exactly as shown. SMTO only switches to a model whose name matches the server's list letter for letter, including any tag after a colon.
  2. If the Gateway is on a different computer from SMTO, open Parameter Store, open your Local AI Runtime profile, and check that the address SMTO's own server should use (the setting named in Technical details) reaches that same model server. Without the right address, SMTO's own server may be reaching a different model server than the one on the Gateway.
  3. Ask SMTO to preview switching to the model again, then apply that new preview. A fresh preview repeats both checks with the corrected name and address.

What success looks like

  • The preview succeeds and lists your model, and after applying it the Main card in Settings › Setup › Model routing shows that model.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't point Main at a different model server just because it answers; it must be the one on your Gateway.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Activation found that the requested model ID is missing from the controller-visible /models inventory, or that the controller-visible and selected-Gateway inventories differ.

What this means

  • Activation compares the requested model with controller-visible inventory and the selected Gateway inventory; the requested identity or inventories disagree. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • Activation compares the requested model with controller-visible inventory and the selected Gateway inventory; the requested identity or inventories disagree.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the requested model ID and both inventories through their intended routes; check that controller loopback is not pointing to another machine's service.

How to fix it

  • Compare the model IDs returned by the controller URL (the profile's controller_base_url, or its endpoint for a loopback Gateway) with local_ai.models on the selected Gateway; they must list the same IDs, including the exact requested model. Fix the model name or controller_base_url so both point at the same server, then create a fresh activation_preview.
  • Correct the controller-reachable route or model selection, then obtain a fresh activation preview.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • Both routes expose the same inventory containing the requested model.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
